name: Question 14
problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=⟨{x}^{2}+{y}^{2},\,1⟩$ and the points $A(1,0)$ and $B(0,1)$ in the $xy$-plane. 

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=0,$ where ${C}_{1}$ is the path along the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1,$ traversed from $A$ to $B$ in counterclockwise direction.
- ${\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=\frac{1}{3},$ where ${C}_{2}$ is the path along line segment $\overset{―}{AB},$ traversed from $A$ to $B.$
- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ is independent of path.
- $F$ is conservative.
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a piecewise-smooth curve given by the vector-valued function $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b].$ Let $f$ be a differentiable function of two or three variables such that $∇f$ is continuous on $C.$ The fundamental theorem for line integrals states that 

$$
{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r=f(r(b))-f(r(a)).
$$

 

This theorem implies that the line integral of a conservative vector field depends only on the value of $f$ at the initial and terminal points $A$ and $B,$ and is independent of the path between them.

With that in mind, we consider each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Parameterizing the circle, we have

$$
{r}_{1}(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}⟨{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}⟨1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})-(\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is true. Parameterizing the line segment, we have

$$
{r}_{2}(t)=⟨1-t,\,t⟩,\,t\in [0,1].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}⟨(1-t)^{2}+{t}^{2},\,1⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,1⟩\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}⟨2{t}^{2}-2t+1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,1⟩\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2t-2{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[{t}^{2}-\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1-\frac{2}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false. Since ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ have the same initial and terminal points, yet

$$
{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r\ne {\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r,
$$

we conclude that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ is path-dependent.

- Statement IV is false. If a vector field is conservative then it is path-independent. Since $F$ is path-dependent, it is not conservative.

∫C∇f⋅dr=f(r(b))−f(r(a)).

This theorem implies that the line integral of a conservative vector field depends only on the value of f at the initial and terminal points A and B, and is independent of the path between them.

With that in mind, we consider each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is true. Parameterizing the circle, we have r1(t)=⟨cos⁡t,sin⁡t⟩,t∈[0,π2]. Therefore, ∫C1F⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫0π/2⟨cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t,1⟩⋅⟨−sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩dt=∫0π/2⟨1,1⟩⋅⟨−sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩dt=∫0π/2−sin⁡t+cos⁡tdt=[cos⁡t+sin⁡t]0π/2=(cos⁡π2+sin⁡π2)−(cos⁡0+sin⁡0)=0.

  • Statement II is true. Parameterizing the line segment, we have r2(t)=⟨1−t,t⟩,t∈[0,1]. Therefore, ∫C2F⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01⟨(1−t)2+t2,1⟩⋅⟨−1,1⟩dt=∫01⟨2t2−2t+1,1⟩⋅⟨−1,1⟩dt=∫012t−2t2dt=[t2−2t33]01=1−23−0=13.

  • Statement III is false. Since C1 and C2 have the same initial and terminal points, yet ∫C1F⋅dr≠∫C2F⋅dr, we conclude that ∫CF⋅dr is path-dependent.
